name: O365 Mass Sharing Link Creation
description: Detection and analysis of abnormal mass sharing link creation in Microsoft 365, SharePoint, or OneDrive.
objective: Detect potential data exposure through abnormal sharing link creation
Identify compromised or misused Microsoft 365 accounts
Prioritize alerts involving sensitive files, unknown sessions or unusual source locations
Recommend containment and investigation actions without replacing analyst validation

recommended_elastic_rule.name: O365 Mass Sharing Link Creation
query_logic: event.outcome, o365.audit.ResultStatus or http.response.status_code indicates a successful action
trigger when the number of matching events is greater than or equal to 25 within 10 minutes

observable_expectations: source.ip should be extracted as an IP observable
destination.ip should be extracted as an IP observable when present
user.email or o365.audit.UserId should be extracted as a mail observable
http.response.status_code and http.request.method should be preserved to confirm successful API activity
user_agent.original or o365.audit.UserAgent should be preserved to identify the client used
file.name, file.path or o365.audit.ObjectId should be preserved as file/object context
sharing.count should be preserved to support volume-based classification
source.geo.country_name, device.name, session.status and data.sensitivity should be available for triage context
analysis_steps: Confirm that the alert is related to SharePoint, OneDrive or Microsoft 365 file sharing
Confirm that the operation succeeded using event.outcome, o365.audit.ResultStatus or http.response.status_code
Check the number of sharing links created and compare it with the rule threshold
Check whether the sharing scope is anonymous, external, company-wide or internal only
Check whether sensitive, confidential or finance-related files are involved
Check the source IP, geolocation and whether they are expected for the user
Check the HTTP method, status code and user-agent/client application
Check whether the device, session or authentication context is known and valid
Check whether multiple files, folders or recipients are involved
Review recent sign-in activity for the same user
Use Cortex or MISP enrichment for source IP, domain or URL observables when available
If enrichment is missing, do not assume the IP, domain or URL is malicious
Determine whether the alert suggests accidental sharing, policy violation, suspicious activity or confirmed data exposure

normal: Sharing volume is below or close to the expected threshold for the user's role
Sharing is internal only or matches an approved business process
No sensitive files or external exposure are involved
No suspicious enrichment result is present
suspicious: Sharing volume is clearly above normal but exposure is not confirmed
Sensitive file names or labels are present but external access is not confirmed
External or anonymous sharing is suspected but recipient scope is incomplete
No confirmed malicious indicator is available
malicious: Very high number of sharing links created in a short time window
Sensitive or confidential files are confirmed as externally exposed
Anonymous or external links are created for sensitive content
Unknown device or suspicious session combined with unusual source location
Multiple countries, impossible travel or clear account compromise evidence
Confirmed malicious IP, anonymized infrastructure or known attacker infrastructure
Evidence shows unauthorized data exposure or post-compromise activity

normal: Close the alert as benign after documenting the business justification
Keep the event for audit trail
suspicious: Keep or create a SOC investigation ticket
Validate the activity with the user, manager or data owner
Review recent Microsoft 365 sign-in activity for the user
Check the list of shared files, recipients and link scopes
Run enrichment on source IP, domain and URL observables when available
Monitor the user account for repeated sharing or unusual sign-in activity
Recommend removal of unnecessary external links if the business need is not confirmed
malicious: Disable or suspend the user account if compromise is likely
Force password reset and MFA re-authentication
Revoke active Microsoft 365 sessions and refresh tokens
Remove suspicious sharing links and external permissions
Identify exposed files, recipients and download activity
Preserve audit logs and investigation evidence
Investigate mailbox, OneDrive, SharePoint and lateral activity
Notify SOC, data owner and Incident Response
Escalate as a data exposure incident

false_positive_considerations: Bulk collaboration during a legitimate project
Migration or reorganization of SharePoint libraries
Approved sharing by HR, finance, legal or project teams
Service account or automation creating expected sharing links
Repeated edits to the same shared object counted as multiple events
limitations: The alert may not include the complete list of recipients or link scopes
The rule detects abnormal sharing volume but does not prove data download
A missing enrichment result must not be interpreted as benign activity
User role and business justification often require human validation
